title: Street fairs, malls and marketplaces, oh my!
content: I have had mall-oriented dreams as far back as I can remember; and while I've never had a large number of dreams that I later couldn't distinguish from actual memories, most of those fitting that description were about malls. A lot of this is quite understandable and even mundane: as a child in the '70s and '80s, we lived in the smaller Tucson, Arizona, but spent time visiting family in Phoenix, where Metrocenter was the newly-built, state-of-the-art, biggest shopping-center in the western world. It only stood to reason that I'd dream about it. That being said, the amount of time I'd spend dreaming of malls and marketplaces has always seemed to suggest a more profound - even *cosmic* \- significance. Then, at some point along the line, I became aware of the concept of 'dreamwalking' aka "shared dreaming", so I find myself both surprised and \*not surprised\* that a rather large contingent of fellow dreamers have converged here in this sub looking for clues and answers to the similar questions we find ourselves asking. ARIZONA A number of times, I have visited a non-existent town in southern Arizona. It's in the same space that the real town of Casa Grande occupies. My most significant visit to the place was during a crowded street-fair/festival. In the parking-lot of a small shopping center that had a laundromat adjacent to a small hotel; were many booths featuring arts and crafts - and FOOD - a pretty Middle-Eastern girl smiled as she handed me a delicious kebab of some kind, and I was very sad that I couldn't have dozens of them to take with me. I learned that the town had the bizarre name of "Pnelle" - pronounced "Thnelle". A lot of this was very atypical for me: I typically don't remember names - particularly proper names of people or places from my dreams - especially their spellings. It wasn't until my next visit to the place that I learned how it was spelled, and that was from a roadside sign designating the town limits. One of those green signs with reflective white lettering. I often have trouble reading in dreams - usually it's something like a newspaper or my phone's screen that I'm trying to decipher, only it appears blurry, or with extra words or symbols over the important areas. I've read that the cause of this is that the part of our brains that we use for reading/visual communication is literally asleep during this particular mode of dream-time. SO - considering that, it's extra-special (to me) whenever I can take \*anything\* of that nature from the dream-world into the waking one. I have met people in subsequent visits who don't seem to have gotten the memo about the town's proper pronunciation; "We live right here in Puh-nell," one of them once said to me. Interestingly, Pnelle (and it's real-world counterpart, Casa Grande) are in the county of Pinal. I would find this even more interesting if I'd dreamed about it without knowing the names of the counties in Arizona, but having grown up here, I just can't claim that the name came from the dream-realm. But let's dig a little, shall we? Pinal county is said to have gotten its name from the Pinal Apaches, of the "pine-clad Pinal Mountains". Melatonin - is secreted by the pineal gland, and is thought by many to produce vivid, weird dreams. This is something I \*did\* know before my first visit to the town and street fair, but I must say - what a wildly convoluted way for my subconscious - if indeed it was - to hint to me that I was visiting a special, shared space. I have also found myself in the spot again - several times since the initial visit during the festival - and while I was disappointed not to find any sort of cultural gathering, I was somewhat intrigued to see that the area looked like it would at the actual time of night that I was having the dream. A dark and mostly deserted highway exit, or quiet hotel lobby. I've recently started wondering if such conditions may possibly be the onset of an OBE/AP via unintentional LD. What I do find myself speculating about more and more, is the possibility that there are more "shared channels" that we can visit while we dream, where we \*receive\* info from external sources - as opposed to the common belief systems that have the entirety of information that our dreams consist of being generated completely from within - our brains just regurgitating their daily experiences back at us.
